You are philosopher 1 of 5 at a round table. You use fork 1 on your left and fork 2 on your right; philosophers 5 and 2 share them with you. You eat 18 meals, one at a time, and you may eat only while you hold both of your forks.

Protocol. Forks are handed out by the arbitrator, node 6. To ask for your forks, send the message 'hungry' to node 6. If node 6 sends you 'eat', you hold both forks: do your next uneaten meal, then send 'done meal K: ANSWER' to node 6 (K is the meal number). That message gives both forks back and, if you have meals left, also asks for your forks again, so do not send 'hungry' with it. If node 6 sends you 'denied', send 'hungry' to node 6 again. Once you have sent 'done' for meal 18, you are finished: send nothing more and end every later turn with 'Decision: WAIT'. Only the arbitrator finishes the run.

You are the arbitrator for 5 philosophers (nodes 1 to 5) at a round table with 5 forks. Each philosopher must eat 18 meals.
Philosopher 1 uses forks 1 and 2.
Philosopher 2 uses forks 2 and 3.
Philosopher 3 uses forks 3 and 4.
Philosopher 4 uses forks 4 and 5.
Philosopher 5 uses forks 5 and 1.
All forks start free.

Protocol. When philosopher i sends 'hungry': if both of its forks are free, they are now held by philosopher i; send 'eat' to node i. Otherwise send 'denied' to node i. When philosopher i sends 'done meal K: ANSWER', both of its forks are free again and its meal K is eaten. If it has meals left, that message also asks for its forks again: answer it as you would 'hungry' from philosopher i. If it has eaten all 18, send nothing (Decision: WAIT). Never let a fork be held by two philosophers at once. When all 5 philosophers have eaten 18 meals each (90 in all), finish the run: put every philosopher's meal answers, in order, between <answer> and </answer>, and end with 'Decision: DONE'.
